title: Flat coefficient restriction and normalized derived operations on module diagrams
statement:
Let $J$ be a small category, and let $\mathcal C_U,\mathcal C_V$ be small sites in the module-sheaf universe. Let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_U)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_V)$ be a geometric morphism, that is an adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ with $u^{-1}$ preserving finite limits [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. On each site $T=U,V$ let $a_T:R_T\to S_T$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings. Suppose $S_T$ is flat over $R_T$, meaning $S_T\otimes_{R_T}-$ is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Specify ring isomorphisms $c_R:u^{-1}R_V\simeq R_U$ and $c_S:u^{-1}S_V\simeq S_U$ satisfying $a_Uc_R=c_Su^{-1}a_V$. Put $\mathcal A_{T,R}=\operatorname{Fun}(J,\operatorname{Mod}(R_T))$ and $\mathcal A_{T,S}=\operatorname{Fun}(J,\operatorname{Mod}(S_T))$, with module sheaves as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and diagram-site models as in [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. Let $r_T$ be termwise restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $L_R,L_S$ be termwise inverse image with the ring action transported by $c_R,c_S$, and $F_R,F_S$ termwise module direct image, whose action uses the adjoint ring map. Use the termwise module adjunctions $L_R\dashv F_R$, $L_S\dashv F_S$. Write $D$ for localization of cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; derive exact functors termwise and derive $F_R,F_S$ by K-injective resolutions, where K-injective means every map from an acyclic complex is null-homotopic [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Use the derived adjunctions normalized by [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general].

Restriction $r_T$ is exact and preserves K-injective diagram complexes. There are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$b:r_UL_S\xrightarrow{\sim}L_Rr_V,\qquad d:r_VRF_S\xrightarrow{\sim}RF_Rr_U.$$
Here $b$ is the termwise identified inverse image on underlying abelian sheaves. For a K-injective complex $I$ in $\mathcal A_{U,S}$, $r_UI$ computes the restricted object's derived image, and $d_{QI}$ is induced by the underived identity $r_VF_SI=F_Rr_UI$ with its identified ring actions; $Q$ is localization. These comparisons respect adjuncts: for $M\in D(\mathcal A_{V,S})$, $N\in D(\mathcal A_{U,S})$, and $t:L_SM\to N$ with adjunct $t^\sharp:M\to RF_SN$, the adjunct of $r_U(t)b_M^{-1}$ is $d_Nr_V(t^\sharp)$. The comparisons are isomorphisms of derived diagram functors, including all $J$-transition maps.

proof.text: Restriction is exact: use sheafification and the underlying abelian-sheaf functor to prove preservation of finite limits and colimits, then lift these properties to diagram categories by whiskering. This is proved directly in Lean.

Obtain an additive finite-limit-preserving scalar-extension left adjoint separately on U and V. Whisker its adjunction by J. The left adjoint preserves finite colimits by adjunction and finite limits pointwise, so the right-adjoint K-injective criterion proves K-injective preservation for both restrictions.

Obtain the normalized ordinary comparisons b0 and d0. Construct rU and rV using the exact functor mapDerivedCategory, with its canonical factor isomorphisms. Conjugate Q(b0) by qLS,qU,qV,qLR and descend this isomorphism through the localization fully faithful precomposition functor. The component formula for liftNatIso proves the inverse normalization equation.

Form delta as the mate of b inverse. The derived-mate lemma proves its invertibility and direct normalization. Set d=asIso(delta). The general unit-mate identity, followed by naturality, proves the adjunct equation for every M,N,t. Package these constructions with the preceding exactness and K-injective proofs.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q24-9e0979442 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, its 10 steps, every cited node's statement, the parent lem-weil-pbc-strict-tower-exchange-mate-normalization (steps 5-7 apply this item), the main-20261015 completed-exchange-coherence proof.md, and the Stacks sources 08BJ, 070K, 070I, 070Y, 0FND, 0DVC, 03CZ, 03D3 and 03DA, with labels checked against tags/tags. The statement is true and matches the parent's coefficient category: L_B is u^{-1} with its action transported through an isomorphism c_B, F_B is u_* with its action through the adjoint ring map, all on diagram-site module categories. Flatness is needed: with R=Z and S=Z/p on a point site, the complex Z/p is K-injective over Z/p but not over Z. Edge cases J empty, zero rings and u=id behave correctly. It is not a duplicate of lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction (single pro-etale sites, no flatness, no diagrams; neither specializes to the other) and not a restated parent clause. Steps 1-6, 8 and 10 check: the coefficient square gives linearity of b^0, rho_R and rho_S are adjuncts of the two equal composites, the unit identity follows from the transport node's underlying-Hom clause, and 08BJ applies to E_T -| r_T (exact by flatness) and to L_B -| F_B (exact because u^{-1} preserves finite limits). The one gap, C2/E5 type: step 9 applied the representative formula of lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general without constructing the representing essentially-constant cocone and cone that the formula requires. I fixed this in step 7: p_s=RF(Qs)^{-1}beta_{I'} with rho=beta_{I_0}^{-1}RF(Qs_0), and I checked the transition identity QF_h(a) rho p_s = QF_h(c). Dually u_t=QG(t)^{-1}phi_M with r=phi_M^{-1}. Step 7's uses now include def-pc-essentially-constant-ind-diagram and def-pc-essentially-constant-pro-diagram (definitions, so notions rather than route) and lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general, and proof_deps is recomputed as the union. I accept the declared tool uses prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist (generic K-injective resolutions) and lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general (the normalization the statement fixes).
